record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: In what varieties of ℓ-groups is the ℓ-subgroup generated by the factors always their free product?

evidence.quote: 1.37. (W. B. Powell, C. Tsinakis [78]) In what varieties of ℓ-groups is the ℓ-subgroup generated by the factors always their free product?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is an algebraic structure (G, ·, ∧, ∨) such that (G, ·) is a group, (G, ∧, ∨) is a lattice, and the group operation distributes over the lattice operations on both sides. A variety V of ℓ-groups is a class of ℓ-groups closed under taking ℓ-subgroups, ℓ-homomorphic images, and arbitrary direct products (equivalently, defined by a set of identities in the language {·, ⁻¹, e, ∧, ∨}). Given a family {G_i}_{i∈I} of ℓ-groups in V, their free product in V is the coproduct in V: an ℓ-group F in V together with ℓ-group embeddings ι_i : G_i → F such that for any ℓ-group H in V and any family of ℓ-homomorphisms φ_i : G_i → H there is a unique ℓ-homomorphism Φ : F → H with Φ ∘ ι_i = φ_i for all i.

For a family {G_i}_{i∈I} of ℓ-groups in V, embedded canonically into the free product F = ∗_V G_i via the maps ι_i, let ⟨G_i : i ∈ I⟩ denote the ℓ-subgroup of F generated by the union of the images ι_i(G_i). Trivially F = ⟨G_i : i ∈ I⟩ as ℓ-groups, but in a sub-ℓ-group of an arbitrary ℓ-group containing isomorphic copies of the G_i, the ℓ-subgroup they generate need not coincide with their free product in V.

Characterize the varieties V of ℓ-groups with the following property: for every ℓ-group H in V and every family {G_i}_{i∈I} of ℓ-subgroups of H, the ℓ-subgroup of H generated by ⋃_{i∈I} G_i is (canonically isomorphic to) the free product in V of the family {G_i}_{i∈I}.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaced several papers by Powell and Tsinakis on free products in varieties of ℓ-groups (including their 1989 chapter "Free products in varieties of lattice-ordered groups"), but no source explicitly resolving the characterization problem of which varieties have the property that the ℓ-subgroup generated by a family of factors always coincides with their free product. Status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Powell, Tsinakis: Free products in the class of abelian ℓ-groups
status_evidence.snippet: Powell and Tsinakis studied free products in the variety of abelian ℓ-groups.
status_evidence.claim: Relevant background work by the authors of the question on free products in specific varieties; no general characterization given.

status_evidence.title: Ordered Algebraic Structures (Powell, Tsinakis eds.)
status_evidence.snippet: Volume containing Powell-Tsinakis chapter 'Free products in varieties of lattice-ordered groups.'
status_evidence.claim: Authors have a chapter surveying free products in varieties, but the general characterization problem appears not resolved there.
